task_title: Floor 5 Slice 5: Ratings Ram lifecycle and atomic breach

plan_review.notes: Approved with changes. Alt A barrier-sealed seam adopted because the generator already carves the ingress and BarrierRegistry.version drives renderer invalidation; sealed-generator tile mutation was rejected because it duplicates terrain redraw/collision state; a monolithic scenario-objective implementation was rejected in favor of a dedicated siegeRamSystem for runtime movement with director/objective-tick authority for phase and post-damage resolution. Resolutions: create a poly wall barrier at init and drop it atomically with wall/ram/marker retirement; fold barriers.version into cached AI navigation signatures instead of inventing a parallel revision; derive route waypoints and a traversable attack anchor from semantic layout landmarks; remove outer-wall from minion targets and reject non-ram wall damage; order damage, HP sync, base defeat, wall-vs-ram resolution (wall lethal wins after base precedence), breach commit, rebuild scheduling, then goals/trace; test reachability through findTilePath, not raw tile flags.

findings.detail: The stated 5-apple Ratings Ram lifecycle and atomic breach task is entirely unimplemented; the graded tree changes only the ledger and contains no runtime or test changes.
The ledger records completed code-review stages for a code-free diff, so those stages cannot serve as clean evidence for the stated gameplay task.
The committed ledger still lacks its independent-grade record and therefore fails validation until this grade is recorded.
The stated 5-apple implementation also lacks its required handoff, apple record, runtime observation, and deterministic regression evidence.

independent_grade.notes: Graded strictly against the stated task, the one-file ledger diff delivers none of the Ratings Ram runtime behavior or tests. The JSON and plan notes are readable, but the correct independent verdict is fail and human escalation rather than fabricated cleanliness.
